title: How do we copy an angle with a protractor?
description: A given angle is measured with a protractor, and a new angle with the same number of degrees is drawn from a fresh base ray. The new angle is measured again as a check, and the steps are written down.
teaching_notes: One idea: to copy an angle, first measure it, then draw a new angle with that number of degrees. Watch for students who copy the angle by eye and do not measure it.

video_script.why: The child measures a given angle and then draws a new angle of that measure, using the steps for drawing an angle that were learnt with the thirty degree example.
video_script.substitution: The angle IHJ of the book's question.
video_script.anchor: the angle IHJ of the book, with the protractor beside it
video_script.payoff_line: Measure angle eye aitch jay, then draw an angle of that measure

final_answer.value: Measure angle IHJ with a protractor, then draw an angle of that measure, following the steps of the example
final_answer.spoken: draw an angle of that measure

maths_rules: measure angle IHJ: the centre on H, one arm on a zero line, read the scale that starts at zero on that arm
draw a new base ray, put the centre on its vertex and the base ray along the zero line
mark the point at the measure found, and join it to the vertex with a ruler
check: the new angle measures the same number of degrees as angle IHJ
video_script.design: The given angle stays on the board. It is measured first, then a new angle is built beside it in four steps, and the check puts the protractor over both angles in turn.
open_questions: The figure is not in the extracted text, so the measure of angle IHJ is not given. The worklist note of about forty degrees by eye is not used, and the video states no number for it.
